mn147:0.2: The Shorter Discourse of Advice to Rāhula
mn147:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn147:1.3: Then, while the Blessed One was alone in meditation, a thought arose in his mind thus:
mn147:1.4: “The states that ripen in deliverance have ripened in Rāhula.
mn147:1.5: Suppose I were to lead him on further to the destruction of the taints.”
mn147:1.6: Then, when it was morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, went into Sāvatthī for alms.
mn147:1.7: When he had walked for alms in Sāvatthī and had returned from his almsround, after his meal he addressed the venerable Rāhula thus:
mn147:1.8: “Take your sitting cloth with you, Rāhula;
mn147:1.9: let us go to the Blind Men’s Grove to pass the day.”
mn147:1.10: “Yes, venerable sir,” the venerable Rāhula replied, and taking his sitting cloth with him, he followed close behind the Blessed One.
mn147:2.1: Now on that occasion many thousands of deities followed the Blessed One, thinking:
mn147:2.2: “Today the Blessed One will lead the venerable Rāhula further to the destruction of the taints.”
mn147:2.3: Then the Blessed One went into the Blind Men’s Grove and sat down at the root of a certain tree on a seat made ready.
mn147:2.4: And the venerable Rāhula paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down at one side.
mn147:2.5: The Blessed One then said to the venerable Rāhula:
mn147:2.7: Is the eye permanent or impermanent?”
mn147:2.9: “Is what is impermanent suffering or happiness?”
mn147:2.11: “Is what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change fit to be regarded thus:
mn147:2.12: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”

mn147:9.1: “Seeing thus, Rāhula, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye, disenchanted with forms, disenchanted with eye-consciousness, disenchanted with eye-contact, and disenchanted with anything comprised within the feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness that arise with eye-contact as condition.
mn147:9.2: He becomes disenchanted with the ear, disenchanted with sounds…
mn147:9.3: disenchanted with the nose, disenchanted with odours…
mn147:9.4: disenchanted with the tongue, disenchanted with flavours…
mn147:9.5: disenchanted with the body, disenchanted with tangibles…
mn147:9.6: He becomes disenchanted with the mind, disenchanted with mind-objects, disenchanted with mind-consciousness, disenchanted with mind-contact, and disenchanted with anything comprised within the feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness that arise with mind-contact as condition.
mn147:9.7: Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion [his mind] is liberated. When it is liberated there comes the knowledge: ‘It is liberated.’
mn147:9.8: He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more coming to any state of being.’”
mn147:9.9: That is what the Blessed One said.
mn147:9.10: The venerable Rāhula was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
mn147:9.11: Now while this discourse was being spoken, through not clinging the venerable Rāhula’s mind was liberated from the taints.
mn147:9.12: And in those many thousands of deities there arose the spotless immaculate vision of the Dhamma:
mn147:9.13: “All that is subject to arising is subject to cessation.”
